official.deadline_note: Each partner in the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program sets their own deadline. Please check the Program website of the partner institution(s) of your choice for the specific deadline.
official.application_cycle: Ongoing programme, published period August 2012-Ongoing; applications run on each partner institution's own admissions schedule
official.status_note: The programme page lists Status: active and Period: August 2012-Ongoing. There is no central application window or intake date; each partner institution runs its own admissions cycle.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program provides financial, psychosocial, and academic support to Scholars. Financial support includes, but is not limited to, tuition fees, accommodation, books and other scholastic materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development, and a return air ticket to a Mastercard Foundation Scholar's country of origin if necessary.
benefits: A return air ticket to a Mastercard Foundation Scholar's country of origin, if necessary
Reimbursement of admission application fees if the candidate is selected, for institutions that require them
eligibility: Apply directly through a Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program-affiliated partner institution or non-governmental organization
Scholarships are offered at secondary, undergraduate and master's levels; scholarships are not currently available to PhD/doctoral candidates
The programme specifically emphasizes recruiting young women, persons with disabilities, and forcibly displaced young people; refugees and displaced populations can qualify
Published admissions criteria include academic excellence, leadership, financial need, and intention to use the programme experience to give back to society
Majors and degrees eligible vary by partner institution; partner institutions serve young people from underrepresented backgrounds
requirements: Meet the chosen partner institution's own admission requirements for the programme of interest
Follow that partner's own application process, timelines, guidelines and fees
Where a North American university requires TOEFL and/or SAT scores as part of the application process for international candidates, provide the relevant test scores
Pay any admission application fee the partner requires; the fees will be reimbursed if the candidate is selected for the programme
documents: Documents required by the chosen partner institution's own admissions process
TOEFL and/or SAT scores where a North American partner university requires them for international candidates
selection_criteria: Intention to use the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program experience to give back to society
coverage: A return air ticket to a Mastercard Foundation Scholar's country of origin, if necessary
application_method: Identify a Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program-affiliated institution from the programme's Where To Apply listings
Read the partner's application guidelines or contact the institution for its deadlines, admission fees and requirements
Apply directly through the partner institution's own application process; candidates can apply to as many universities as they wish
Await the partner's decision; the application process and decision-making are managed individually by each partner, not by the Foundation
official.application_route: Apply directly to an affiliated partner institution or NGO through that partner's own admissions process; the partner manages the application process and decision-making.
official.international_eligibility: Applicants apply through partner institutions wherever they are located; partners are primarily in Africa, but the Foundation also has partners in North and Central America, Europe, and the Middle East, and each partner sets its own geographic eligibility.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Majors and degrees eligible for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program vary by partner; eligible majors at a specific partner are published in that partner's application instructions.
official.duration: Programme period published as August 2012-Ongoing; study duration follows each partner institution's degree programme at the secondary, undergraduate or master's level.
official.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a global initiative designed to develop the next generation of transformative leaders by enabling highly talented, service-oriented young people to pursue higher education and cultivate their leadership potential. The Foundation describes it as the largest scholarship initiative of its kind in Africa, focused on enabling talented and diverse young people, particularly young women, to lead, pursue their aspirations and enrich their communities. It provides financial, social and academic support delivered through a pan-African and global network of partner universities and NGOs.
official.region: Global - partner institutions are primarily in Africa, with partners also in North and Central America, Europe and the Middle East
official.program_type: Foundation scholarship programme implemented through partner universities and non-governmental organizations

applicant_utility.summary: There is no single application to this scholarship: you must shortlist an affiliated partner institution and apply through its own admissions process, on its deadline, with its document list. The Foundation publishes no fixed award amount because support is defined institution by institution, but it confirms that tuition fees, accommodation, books and other scholastic materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development and, if necessary, a return air ticket home are covered. Selection rests on academic excellence, leadership, financial need and a credible plan to give back to society, and admission to a partner does not by itself guarantee the scholarship. PhD and doctoral candidates are not currently eligible, so this route fits secondary, undergraduate and master's applicants.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Service-oriented young people from underrepresented backgrounds - especially young women, persons with disabilities, and forcibly displaced young people - who can win a place through an affiliated partner at secondary, undergraduate or master's level.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist two or three affiliated partners whose eligible majors, location and admission route genuinely fit you, starting only from the Foundation's Where To Apply listings.
Open each partner's own admissions page and record its exact deadline, required documents and application fee before drafting anything.
Build evidence for the published selection pillars - academic excellence, leadership, financial need and giving back to society - into your essays and references, not just your grades.

If your target partner is in North America, budget and book TOEFL/SAT months ahead; the Foundation notes these costs are a barrier for many applicants and points to Education USA as a possible source of test-cost support.
Do not let an admission application fee stop you where it is genuinely unaffordable - the Foundation states the fee is reimbursed if the candidate is selected.
common_rejection_risks: Sending an application to the Foundation itself - there is no central portal, and packages are not considered through the Foundation.
Assuming admission equals funding: gaining admission to a partner institution does not guarantee selection, which the Foundation calls highly competitive.
Tracking the Foundation's news page instead of the partner's own admissions calendar and missing the partner's deadline.
A grade-only application that does not evidence leadership, community contribution and financial need, which partners explicitly assess.
Submitting without the TOEFL and/or SAT scores a North American partner requires for international candidates.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Admission application fees (reimbursed only if you are selected) and TOEFL/SAT test costs where a partner requires them; the Foundation publishes no coverage for visas, initial travel to the partner institution or day-to-day personal expenses.
document_audit: Every partner defines its own document list, so transcript formats, reference letters and essay requirements differ from institution to institution - never reuse one partner's package unchanged for another.
TOEFL/SAT scores must be booked early where a North American partner requires them for international candidates; late scores arrive after the decision.
Keep proof of payment for any admission application fee, since reimbursement depends on being selected.

Applicants without conventional academic records, including displaced applicants, should contact their chosen partner directly and early - the Foundation states exceptions cannot be made outside the partner-led process.
alerts: The Foundation warns of Facebook posts and groups advertising recruitment for this programme and requesting an application fee; it states these groups are not associated with it, that it never solicits funding or requests payments from individuals, and asks that suspected fraud be reported to local law enforcement and to ethics@mastercardfdn.org.
There is no central deadline and no central status tracker - application status questions must go to the partner institution directly.
PhD/doctoral candidates are not currently eligible, and the Foundation does not sponsor or financially support candidates who are not awarded a scholarship through the programme.
The Foundation is not accepting unsolicited partnership proposals, so new partners are announced only through its own news channels.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Choose an affiliated partner, follow its published admissions process and deadline, submit the full partner application package including any fee, then wait for the partner's decision - the partner, not the Foundation, selects scholars.
